action.use_results: Use these values in the settings
banner.no_auth: The web UI has no username and password: anyone who reaches it can change the fans.
banner.scanning: Looking for the sensor chips (sensors-detect), this can take a minute…
banner.truenas_hint: On TrueNAS SCALE, load it on the host: System → Advanced Settings → Init/Shutdown Scripts → Add, Type “Command”, Command “modprobe {module}”, When “Post Init”. Run the command once in the TrueNAS shell (or reboot), then press Scan again.
banner.no_pwm: No PWM output was found. The kernel module of the fan chip is probably not loaded.
banner.settings_error: The saved settings have invalid values: the environment variables are used. Check the logs.
banner.waiting: Choose the drives and the fans: the guided setup asks one question at a time, or use Settings.
banner.read_only: Read only: /sys is mounted read only, as in a container that is not privileged. The fans are not controlled, hddfancontrol and hd-idle do not run, manual control and the PWM test are off, and SMART data may not be readable. Run the container with privileged: true (on TrueNAS SCALE: Privileged in the app settings).
banner.missing_pwms: The chip of these fans is not on the host, so they are not controlled: {paths}. Load its kernel module (see Log), or choose the fans again in Settings.
banner.failsafe: No recent drive temperature: every fan runs at full speed until the temperatures come back.
banner.safety: A drive reached the maximum temperature: every fan runs at full speed.
banner.safety_stale: No recent drive temperature in manual control: every fan runs at full speed until you leave manual control.
banner.control_error: The fan control hit an error, so every fan runs at full speed: {error}. See the logs.
overview.no_temps: No temperature yet: hddfancontrol writes them once it runs.
fans.title: Fans
fans.intro: Every PWM output of the host. In manual control, move any slider and watch the speed to find out which fan it drives; each output you move gets its previous setting back when you leave manual control. The curve and auto modes drive only the fans chosen in Settings. Manual control is never saved: a restart goes back to automatic control, and so does closing this page (or putting the computer to sleep) for 2 minutes. A page left open in another tab keeps it.
fans.others_hint: Not chosen in Settings, without a name and not turning: usually empty connectors. Give one a name to keep it above.
fans.safety: A drive reached the maximum temperature: the fans stay at full speed.
fans.safety_stale: No recent drive temperature: the fans stay at full speed. Leave manual control to go back to automatic control.
fans.safety_error: The fan control hit an error: the fans stay at full speed. Leave manual control to go back to automatic control.
smart.title: SMART data
smart.intro: Read with smartctl -n standby: a sleeping drive is not woken, and keeps its last data.
smart.none: No SMART data yet. Only the drives marked as monitored in Settings are read.
smart.asleep_note: The drive was asleep at the last check.
smart.warn.reported_uncorrectable: The drive reported errors it could not correct.
smart.warn.spin_retries: The drive needed retries to spin up.
smart.warn.crc_errors: Interface CRC errors: check the cable.
smart.warn.attribute_failed: An attribute went below its threshold.
smart.failed_past: Went under the threshold in the past, not now: {attributes}. Often the airflow temperature of a drive that once ran hot; worth knowing, not a failure.
smart.warn.worn_out: The drive is almost worn out.
smart.warn.critical_warning: The drive raised a critical warning.
history.empty: No data in this window yet.
history.hint: Point at a chart to read the values; click a name to hide or show its line. Fans that are not used are hidden at first.
settings.source_file: These settings were saved from the web UI.
settings.source_environment: These settings come from the environment variables. Saving them here stores them in /config/settings.json, which then wins.
settings.mode_help_curve: Curve: hddfancontrol runs the fans at the minimum speed up to the minimum temperature, at full speed from the maximum temperature, and in proportion in between. The target is not used.
settings.mode_help_auto: Auto: a feedback controller keeps the hottest drive near the target with as little fan speed as it needs, and adapts to load, season and case by itself. From the maximum temperature the fans run at full speed. The minimum temperature is not used.
settings.min_speed_warning: Set the minimum speed to 0 only if other fans cool the case, or the case is built for passive cooling.
settings.drives_help: Fans: the drives whose temperature drives the fans and that hd-idle spins down. Monitored: the drives whose SMART data is read and shown in Drives. Use the stable names of /dev/disk/by-id.
settings.other_drives_help: Paths or interface names (ata, nvme), separated by spaces.
settings.fans_help: The PWM outputs to control, with the value at which each fan starts and stops. The PWM test finds them.
settings.spin_down_help: 0 turns hd-idle off. A drive's own value, in the drive list, wins; 0 there keeps that drive spinning.
settings.spin_down_command_help: ata for SATA drives, scsi for SAS drives and some USB enclosures.
settings.hwmons_help: Also run the fans for these sensors: in proportion between the minimum and the maximum, at full speed from the maximum. Without a range, hddfancontrol picks one in the curve mode, and the auto mode ignores the sensor. Avoid CPU sensors unless the CPU uses little power.
settings.restore_fan_settings: When hddfancontrol stops, give the fans back their previous settings (otherwise they run at full speed)
settings.reset_done: The environment variables are used again.
pwmtest.title: PWM test
pwmtest.intro: Finds, for each fan, the PWM value at which it starts turning and the one at which it stops. Choose the outputs to test.
pwmtest.warning: During the test, fan control stops and each tested fan stops several times. It takes a few minutes per fan. Fan control starts again at the end, or when you cancel.
pwmtest.review: Values copied. Check them and save.
security.title: Username and password
security.state_none: The web UI is open. Set a username and a password to protect it.
security.state_environment: The web UI is protected by WEBUI_USERNAME and WEBUI_PASSWORD (user {username}). Change them in the container settings.
security.saved: Saved. Other sessions have been logged out.
security.removed: Protection removed: the web UI is open.
labels.label: Name
error.invalid_label_key: Only drives and fans can be named.
error.invalid_label: A name has at most 40 printable characters.
error.invalid_drive: Not a /dev path or an interface name.
error.range_order: Must be higher than the minimum.
error.range_both: Set both the minimum and the maximum, or neither.
error.unknown_drive: Not one of the chosen drives.
error.target_order: Must be lower than the maximum temperature.
error.unreadable_file: The settings file cannot be read.
error.busy: A PWM test or a scan is running. Wait until it ends.
error.save_failed: Cannot write to /config. Is the volume writable?
error.invalid_json: The request is not valid JSON.
error.too_many_attempts: Too many wrong passwords from this address: try again in 15 minutes.
error.auth_from_env: The credentials come from the environment variables and cannot be changed here.
error.invalid_username: The username cannot be empty or contain ':'.
error.password_too_short: The password needs at least 8 characters.
error.unknown_pwm: This PWM output does not exist on the host.
error.read_only: /sys is read only (the container is not privileged): the fans cannot be written.
error.network: The web UI cannot reach the server.
lang.label: Language
wizard.welcome_text: A few questions and your drive fans run on their own. Nothing changes until the last step.
wizard.welcome_1: Choose the drives to keep cool.
wizard.welcome_2: Find out which fans blow on them, and choose those.
wizard.welcome_3: Measure the fans (optional) and choose how cool to keep the drives.
wizard.welcome_4: Decide whether idle drives may sleep, and protect this page with a password.
wizard.welcome_safe: You can close the guided setup at any time and open it again from the header; everything can be changed later in Settings.
wizard.read_only: The container cannot write the fan settings (/sys is read only): it is not privileged. Set privileged: true in the app's YAML, deploy it again, then come back here.
wizard.no_pwm: No fan output was found. The sensor chip module may be missing: see the message above, load it, then open the guided setup again.
wizard.drives_text: Their temperature sets the fan speed: the hottest of them wins. Hard drives are already ticked; SSDs and NVMe drives usually do not need it.
wizard.drives_hint: Only these drives are read, and a sleeping drive is never woken up to read its temperature.
wizard.no_drives: No drive found. Is /dev mounted in the container?
wizard.fans_text: Each line is a fan connector of the motherboard. Not sure which is which? Press Identify: that fan runs at full speed for 10 seconds; listen, or watch its RPM rise. Give it a name if you like.
wizard.fans_cpu: Do not choose the CPU fan: its speed would follow the drives, not the processor.
wizard.fans_hint: A fan at 0 RPM may be stopped, or its connector may have no speed sensor: Identify tells you.
wizard.measure_text: Every fan model starts and stops at different values. The test finds them by slowing each chosen fan down until it stops; it takes a few minutes per fan, and each tested fan stops several times. You can cancel it at any time.
wizard.measure_skip: If you skip it, safe values are used (start {start}, stop {stop}): the fans never go very slow. You can run the test later from the PWM test tab.
wizard.measure_running: Test running: the fans speed up and slow down, that is normal.
wizard.temps_title: How cool should the drives be?
wizard.temps_text: Under the lower value the fans run at their minimum; at the upper one, at full speed; in between, the speed follows the temperature.
wizard.temps_hint: Most hard drives are rated up to 55–60 °C; they last longer under 45 °C.
wizard.preset_quiet_text: The fans stay slow until {min} °C: less noise, warmer drives.
wizard.preset_balanced_text: Speed rises from {min} °C and is full at {max} °C.
wizard.preset_cool_text: The fans react from {min} °C: cooler drives, more noise.
wizard.spindown_text: A sleeping drive saves power and stays cool, but waking it takes a few seconds, and frequent sleep and wake cycles wear it out.
wizard.spindown_never_text: The drives keep spinning; the system or TrueNAS may still put them to sleep.
wizard.spindown_short_text: For drives that stay unused for hours, such as a backup pool.
wizard.spindown_long_text: A middle way: sleep only after a long pause.
wizard.password_text: Anyone who reaches this page can change the fans. Choose a username and a password (at least 8 characters), or leave the password empty to skip.
wizard.password_hint: You can set or change them later in the Security tab.
wizard.password_set: This page already has a username and password.
wizard.summary_text: Check the choices, then save: hddfancontrol starts at once.
error.no_notify_url: No address is saved: enter one and save the settings first.
error.notify_failed: The message could not be sent: check the address and that the service is reachable from the container (see Logs).
error.invalid_url: Enter an address that starts with http:// or https://.
alert.drive_hot: {drive} is at {temp} °C, at or above the maximum of {max} °C.
alert.fan_stalled: {fan} does not turn: 0 RPM with the PWM at {percent} %. Check the fan and its cable.
alert.smart_failing: {drive}: SMART says the drive is failing. Back up its data and replace it.
alert.safety: No new drive temperature: every fan runs at full speed.
alert.test: Test message from hddfancontrol: notifications work.
settings.notify_help: When a drive gets too hot, a fan stops, SMART reports a problem or the temperatures stop coming in, a message is sent to this address, and another when it is over. Leave it empty for none.
settings.notify_url_help: ntfy: https://ntfy.sh/a-topic-of-yours · Gotify: https://your-server/message?token=… · JSON: any webhook that takes a POST.
alert.fans_missing: The fan chip is not found any more, so these fans are not controlled: {fans}. Choose them again in Settings.
alert.drive_missing: {drive} is not on the host any more: unplugged, dead, or dropped by its controller. Check it, or remove it from the monitored drives in Settings.
alert.smart_error: {drive}: the SMART data cannot be read ({error}).
settings.backup_help: Export saves the settings and the names of drives and fans to a file; import checks such a file, then saves and applies it, as Save and apply does. Fans and drives are kept by path: after moving to another machine, check them.
error.backup_invalid: This file is not a backup of hddfancontrol web UI.
alert.hidden: {count} warnings taken note of are hidden.
alert.hidden_one: 1 warning taken note of is hidden.
drive.smr_hint: SMR (shingled) recording: slow on sustained writes, a poor fit for ZFS and RAID rebuilds.
drive.max_over_limit: The maximum temperature of the settings ({max}) is above the highest this drive recommends ({limit}).
